summary: Elevated first-token latency and intermittent 504s on short chat prompts after runtime/compile swap
description: Customer QuillDocs reports that after last night's runtime/compile backend swap (runtime v2.11 + new kernel selector), short chat prompts that previously returned token(s) within ~80-120ms are now seeing time-to-first-token (TTFB) spikes to 600-1500ms and occasional request 504s. Problem started immediately after the rollout window (2026-03-10 23:30 UTC). Impact: partial degradation for enterprise traffic on dedicated pools in us-west-2; some requests time out. Business impact: affects document assistant features (autosuggest) where perceived latency directly impacts UX. Support ticket opened by customer at 2026-03-11 02:04 UTC.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use customer API key scoped to QuillDocs dedicated pool in us-west-2
2) Send a series of short chat prompts (e.g., 'Summarize this: <10 words>') with streaming enabled and low max_tokens (<=16), 100 concurrent small requests
3) Observe initial bytes delivered and any 504s or long TTFB on a sample of requests
4) Compare same workload against staging pool (runtime v2.10) to confirm regression

Router trace sample: route_id=usw2-router-17 cpu_ms=18 conn_wait_ms=920 kv_cache_hit=false kernel_variant=quant-opt-3
comments: 2026-03-11 02:12 - Maya Chen (Support): Notified SRE and assigned to Liam. Customer reports ~15% of short prompt requests return 504 and many have TTFB > 700ms.

2026-03-11 03:01 - Liam O'Neal (SRE): Reproduced locally against d-qd-01 pool. Observed increased connection waiting time in router traces. Opening profiler on serving-runtime and checking kernel selection behavior.

2026-03-11 06:27 - Elena R. (Runtime Eng): Noted that the kernel selector fallback logic was updated to prefer 'quant-opt-3' for certain sequence-length heuristics in v2.11. Pushed a diagnostic build to log selection metrics.

2026-03-12 10:00 - Maya Chen (Support): Customer confirms regression persists on morning traffic. Provided temporary workaround suggestion to pin model to redwood-llama-3-8b:v2026-02-25 on their dedicated config but customer requests platform fix.

2026-03-13 09:20 - Liam O'Neal (SRE): Narrowed to skew in sequence-length prediction causing runtime to pick a heavier kernel and trigger longer kernel initialization on first token. Drafting mitigation: force warm kernel selection for small prompt bursts and tune router conn_wait timeout.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Kernel selector in runtime v2.11 misclassifies short prompts and selects a quantized kernel path that has a heavy first-call initialization cost (~700-1000ms) even when KV cache is empty.

Hypothesis 2: Router connection scheduling now prefers a 'connect-to-warm' policy that queues requests while kernel init occurs, raising conn_wait_ms and surface 504s when overall queueing exceeds upstream timeout.
Action taken: enabled detailed kernel-selection logging on 3 nodes (usw2-serving-42/43/44) and gathered p50/p95/p99 TTFB per kernel variant for 2 hours starting 2026-03-11T03:00Z.

Finding: quant-opt-3 kernel shows median first-token 880ms and subsequent tokens ~60ms. legacy-opt kernel shows median first-token 120ms. Quant kernel used in ~37% of observed short prompts post-rollout; pre-rollout quant usage was <5% for same customer workload.

Finding: conn_wait_ms for requests that hit the quant-opt-3 kernel correlated strongly (rho=0.82) with elevated TTFB and 504s. Router CPU remained below threshold; queueing originates from per-node kernel init serializing first calls.
Temporary mitigation test: forcing kernel selection to legacy-opt for sample traffic returned TTFB to baseline (p95 160ms) with 0 observed 504s in 15-minute test window.

Next steps: runtime eng to add a short-circuit to prefer 'warm' kernel variants for predicted short prompts, or perform lazy pre-warm of quant kernels during rollout. Also adjust router upstream timeout and backoff for dedicated pools as stop-gap.
resolution: Mitigation in progress. Engineering created PR to change selector fallback heuristics and add an async kernel pre-warm hook (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8761). Temporary customer workaround provided: pin to legacy kernel profile via model config or route small prompt traffic through a canary pool running v2.10. SRE adjusted router conn upstream timeout from 1.5s to 2.5s for QuillDocs dedicated pool to reduce observed 504s while fix lands. Follow-up: post-fix we will run 24h performance validation and coordinate a maintenance window for safe rollout.
